LD 1229: An Act to Create Equity in Maine's Campaign Finance Laws Between Enrolled and Unenrolled Candidates

Good morning Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs,
My name is Al Cleveland, and I am the Advocacy Director of Maine Citizens for Clean Elections. I am
testifying against LD 1229. Maine Citizens for Clean Elections has been the leading campaign finance organization in Maine for over twenty years and one of the nation's most respected state-based
organizations advocating for democratically funded elections. We are proud of our national reputation.
But we are all Mainers, and our nonpartisan mission has always been with and for the people of this
state.
LD 1229 aims to create a level playing field for unenrolled candidates who do not compete in primary elections and therefore only have one election period to raise contributions. As you heard when we testified on LD 390, MCCE shares the goal of fairness for unenrolled candidates, but we support an
alternative policy approach.
Rather than changing the contribution limit, we suggested in prior testimony that the unenrolled candidate should have two election periods, concurrent with the primary and general elections. An
unenrolled candidate that gets an early start and wants to begin campaigning in the spring could raise
funds and begin to build connections and name recognition with voters at the same time as party
candidates are doing the same. During the general election period, the contribution limit would reset for each donor, and the same limit would apply to both party and unenrolled candidates.
Unenrolled candidates who use Clean Elections receive the same amount of funding during the primary
election as the party candidates who have uncontested primary elections. We believe it makes sense to
apply this same standard to privately-financed candidates.
In summary, aligning the contribution limits for unenrolled candidates with the primary and general election would be a fairer approach to all candidates. Thank you for the opportunity to testify. l would be happy to answer any questions from the Committee.

April 7, 2025 - Testimony in support of LD 1229:
An Act to Create Equity in Maine's Campaign Finance Laws Between Enrolled and Unenrolled Candidates
Good morning, Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs. Thank you for the opportunity to testify today. My name is
Representative Billy Bob Faulkingham, and I serve as the House Republican Leader. I represent House District 12, which includes the towns of Franklin, Gouldsboro, Hancock, Sorrento, Sullivan, Winter
Harbor, and Steuben. I am here today to present testimony on my proposed legislation, LD 1229 -An
Act to Create Equity in Maine's Campaign Finance Laws Between Enrolled and Unenrolled
Candidates.
The intent of LD 1229 is simple: to ensure that unenrolled candidates for both gubernatorial and
legislative offices face the same contribution limits as their enrolled counterparts, specifically when those unenrolled candidates are not participating in a primary election. Under the current structure of Maine's campaign finance laws, candidates who are enrolled in a political party face different
contribution limits than unenrolled candidates, which creates an unfair disadvantage for unenrolled candidates, particularly in general elections.
Currently, Maine's campaign finance laws differentiate between candidates based on their
enrollment status. For candidates who are on the ballot in a primary election, both enrolled and
unenrolled candidates face specific contribution limits that are tied to the election cycle. However,
candidates who are not on the ballot in a primary election---typically unenrolled candidates running
in the general election----are limited to a lower contribution cap than their party-enrolled
counterparts. This difference creates an unequal playing field, particularly when it comes to mounting
a competitive and successful campaign.
In short, candidates who are unenrolled face a distinct financial disadvantage compared to their
enrolled peers, and this inequity is especially pronounced in elections where the voter turnout in the primary election is minimal, or the primary has already decided the party nominees. LD 1229 seeks to correct this disparity by ensuring that unenrolled candidates have the same opportunity to raise funds for their campaigns, thereby giving voters a fairer choice in the general election.
Maine has a long tradition ofsupporting independent, unenrolled candidates, with independentminded candidates frequently winning office in both the Legislature and the Governor's Office. The
state has elected independent governors such as Angus King, who served from 1995 to 2003. LD 1229
is consistent with Maine's historic tradition of encouraging a broad range of political expression by ensuring that financial constraints do not inhibit a candidate's ability to run a competitive campaign.

The goal of campaign finance reform should always be to encourage fairness, transparency, and a level playing field. By creating more equitable campaign contribution limits for both enrolled and unenrolled candidates, this bill supports democratic engagement by ensuring that all candidates---- regardless of political affiliation--have an equal opportunity to raise the funds necessary to communicate their message to voters. This is especially important in our modern political environment, where traditional and social media coverage and outreach often require significant
financial resources.

In closing, i urge you to support LD 1229 to create equity in Maine's campaign finance laws. Enrolled
and unenrolled candidates should face the same contribution limits, especially when they are not
participating in primary elections. it will enhance voter choice, foster political diversity, and promote fairness in our electoral system.

l thank you for your time and attention to this important issue, and l respectfully ask for your support
for LD 1229. lam happy to answer any questions you may have.
